delivery_target: Callers of valid_arch_state_global_pd that have valid_arch_state but not pspace_aligned
new_lemma:
lemma valid_arch_state_global_pd':
  "valid_arch_state s
    \<Longrightarrow> obj_at (\<lambda>ko. \<exists>pd. ko = ArchObj (PageDirectory pd)) (arm_global_pd (arch_state s)) s
           \<and> is_aligned (arm_global_pd (arch_state s)) pd_bits"
  apply (clarsimp simp: valid_arch_state_def a_type_def
                        pd_aligned pd_bits_def pageBits_def
                 elim!: obj_at_weakenE)
  apply (clarsimp split: Structures_A.kernel_object.split_asm
                         arch_kernel_obj.split_asm if_split_asm)
  done
rationale: The conjunct `pspace_aligned s` never appears in the proof body of valid_arch_state_global_pd. The proof only uses `valid_arch_state_def`, `a_type_def`, `pd_aligned`, `pd_bits_def`, `pageBits_def`, and case splits — none of which require pspace_aligned as a hypothesis. This is a pure implication lemma making it a high-confidence P-slot candidate.
